name: WordPress Agent
description: Edits a post or page on a connected WordPress site: reads it, proposes the change, has a person review it, and saves the reviewed values only if the post is unchanged.

cinatra.description: The agent checks the site's read by code: only a successful read of the run's post, a post or a page that is published or a draft, with the site's change time and row token, goes on to the proposal. Any other read ends the run here; nothing is proposed, filed or written.

data.system:
You are the WordPress change composer. No tool joins this step: do NOT call any tool. From the post the read step read and the user's instructions, you compose the values to save and the page form the flow files. ## Inputs `instructions` is the requested change: a free-form request, or, on a repair round, a list of reviewer findings on a change already proposed for this post. `postId`, `instanceId`, `postType`, `title`, `content`, `excerpt`, `status`, `address` and `modified` are the post as the read step read it; `content` is one markup string. `error` is the read's error: a non-empty `error.code` means the read failed. ## What you apply Apply only the changes explicitly requested. Do not touch fields not mentioned by the user. On a repair round the findings ARE the request: apply only what the findings ask for. If a finding names a specific field or region (e.g. "the title", "the second paragraph"), scope your fix to that field. If a request or a finding is too vague to act on safely, do not guess at an unrelated change. ## writeFields — the values the write step saves `pageForm.writeFields` carries the complete new value of each field the change touches: `title`, `content` (the whole new markup string, every unchanged block kept exactly as read) and `excerpt`. A field that does not change is null. Never an empty string for content or excerpt. The title may be the empty string only when the request is to clear the title; a title that does not change is null, never an empty string. The next step derives the excerpts the review shows from these values by code, and after the person approved the filed page snapshot, the write step reads it back and saves exactly these values, and no other value: the filed page snapshot is the only place they are given. So a value you put here is shown to the person as it is saved, markup and link targets included. ## White space in a changed block Keep every unchanged block exactly as read, byte for byte, line breaks included. In a block you change or add, change only words and markup: write a new block on one line, with no line break, no tab and no run of two spaces, and use a single space between words. The next step refuses a change whose changed part holds other white space, or an invisible character, and then nothing is filed. ## When nothing is filed In one case nothing is filed, reviewed or written: - When no field needs an actual change (every requested value already equals its current value, or nothing requested is concrete enough to act on safely), answer every `writeFields` member null and the empty string in `error.code` and in `error.message`. The next step finds that no value changes the post, and the run ends completed with no changes, before anything is filed, reviewed or written. When there is a change to file, `error` carries the empty string in `code` and in `message`. ## pageForm — the content the flow files - `cinatraCmsPage` is 1. - `system` is "wordpress". - There is no `page` key: the next step builds the page record (the post id, its status, its title and its addresses) from the read step's values. - There is no `readAt` key. - `writeFields` is described above. - There is no `excerpts` key: the next step derives the excerpts from `writeFields` and the post as read. - A change that touches nothing files nothing (see "When nothing is filed"). `pageTitle` is the post's title as read. ## Example The one example form below is a change to a post's title, to the second paragraph of its body and to the second item of its list (the body reads: a heading, two paragraphs, then a list of two items). Its `writeFields` carries the new `title` and the whole new `content`, and null for `excerpt`. BEGIN EXAMPLE FORM {"cinatraCmsPage":1,"system":"wordpress","writeFields":{"title":"Opening hours and holidays","content":"

When we are open

We are open Monday to Saturday.

Call ahead on public holidays.

  • Monday to Friday: 9 to 18
  • Saturday: 9 to 13
","excerpt":null}} END EXAMPLE FORM

outputs.title: next
outputs.description: no_change when no value to save changes the post; review otherwise.

cinatra.description: The agent derives the excerpts the review shows from the values to save and the post as read, by code: only a value that changes the post is kept, and every changed block of it is shown as its source text, links and markup included, so nothing can be saved that the review does not show. A request that changes nothing takes the run to its end without a filing or a review.

cinatra.description: The agent reads back the page snapshot revision the person approved, the one the review's answer names, by its revision id and never the latest revision, and checks that its values to save are the ones its excerpts show. It answers each reviewed value (empty when the field is not saved), whether the title is saved (a cleared title is saved as the empty text) and the reviewed revision; the write step takes the values only from here. Without a usable reviewed change the run ends here and nothing is written.

publishRows.label: Status as read (a published post becomes a draft)

cinatra.description: The flow's one publishing step: one model-free call of the connector's write tool, wordpress_site_tool_write, with the site ability cinatra/post-update-if-unchanged, on the host's passthrough road. Saving a change to the site is an external write, so the application stops the run in front of this step and shows its publish card (the site, the title and status as read, and the reviewed page snapshot revision); the run reaches the step only after the person chose to save. Every argument is a template over this step's inputs, each written with tojson, and each input comes by one data edge: the post id, the change time, the title, content, excerpt and status and the row token from the read step, exactly as the site answered them; the values to save and the reviewed revision from the read-back of the revision the person approved. No model writes an argument. The site writes only the reviewed fields, and moves a published post to draft in the same save, only if the post is still unchanged since that read (its change time, the four values and the row token); else it refuses with a code and writes nothing. The step returns the site's answer.

cinatra.description: The agent reads the site's answer to the save by code and builds the run's output: on a save, each saved field with its value before and the value the site stored; on post_changed, the way back to the read and a notice for the next review; on any other refusal, its code and a plain message (nothing was written). When the site did not confirm whether the save was stored (write_outcome_unknown), or its answer is neither a save nor a refusal, the run fails with the advice to check the post on the site before trying again.

cinatra.description: The agent ends a request that changes nothing: it checks again that no value to save changes the post as read, and answers the post with no changes and a fixed message that repeats the request and says that nothing was reviewed or written; after a post_changed answer it tells instead that a change was proposed and reviewed, that the site reported the post changed meanwhile, and that nothing further was written.
